grand_strategy.reading: Djibouti sells position. Its state is one port, one railway and a set of rented bases, and its strategy is to be the place every outside power and every landlocked neighbour must pass through, so that no single patron gets it. The threats are the ones that would shrink that position: Ethiopia's search for a sea outlet at Assab, the Berbera project backed by the UAE and Israel, and the Houthi war at the Bab al-Mandab. Water and heat limit any growth beyond rent, and the IGAD seat it hosts is the forum in which it keeps its weight.

stances.note: Defence treaty signed in 2011 and in force from 2014 (National Assembly committee file); renewed on 24 Jul 2024 for twenty years, with the fixed annual payment rising from EUR 30m to EUR 85m; the largest French base abroad (about 1,500 personnel), with the Heron islet to return to Djiboutian control by late 2026. Ratification of the 2024 text is not confirmed in our sources (a bill was on the cabinet agenda on 26 Mar 2025). French chief of defence visit in Jan 2026. Ally by treaty, not by rhetoric. Bond - affinity: our reading of a former colonial power with a long military tie; no source characterises the bond.

stances.note: Ras Doumeira clashes in June 2008 over the border at the Bab al-Mandab; the UN Security Council demanded in 2009 that Eritrea withdraw; a Qatar-brokered accord of 6 Jun 2010 brought the withdrawal, but the border was never demarcated. Friction revived in 2017 (Djibouti alleged an incursion), then a 2018 thaw: Eritrea's foreign minister visited and Djibouti hailed a new era. No source uses the word rival: the grade is our reading of an unsettled border and an open grievance without a stated aim to destroy the regime (confidence C). stances.note: In February 2018 Djibouti seized DP World's Doraleh Container Terminal. The London Court of International Arbitration ruled for DP World; the final award of October 2025 found the seizure unlawful, and Djibouti has refused to pay the awards (about USD 685m) while DP World's 50-year concession stands. DP World is Dubai-based; the state link to the UAE is our reading. Berbera: the UAE's 25-year lease (2017) and DP World's port compete with Djibouti for Ethiopian trade (Crisis Group 2018, the same source the UAE card uses). After Israel recognised Somaliland, Guelleh named the UAE as Israel's main route into the region (2026, reported). Rival, not adversary: competing ports and a live arbitration, no aim to destroy. Trend cooling from the 2026 statements. Bond - none: pure interest.

stances_toward.note: Border legacy: armed clashes at Ras Doumeira (Gabla) and the Doumeira island in June 2008; UN measures on Eritrea from December 2009 (resolution 1907); Qatari mediation from 2010, which ended with Eritrea's pull-back and no demarcation. The 2018 Ethiopian-led thaw did not settle the border. The current alignment runs the other way: Djibouti leans toward Eritrea and Egypt on the Red Sea (Africa Confidential, January 2026), but it earns about USD 1.5bn a year from Ethiopia's use of its port, which is why it is not a partner. Rival, confidence C: the grade is our reading of an unresolved border; no Eritrean or Djiboutian source uses the word. The 2008 casualty figures are contested and not used here.

The strain is the sea-access push: Djibouti offered a 60% stake in the Tadjoura port and, by its account, Addis Ababa declined, wanting a corridor on top of equity (Capital Ethiopia, Apr 2026); Djibouti's own card calls the push an existential risk for it, and fighting in the north in late September 2026 was reported near the routes that link Ethiopia with Djibouti. A dependence in both directions that Ethiopia wants to dilute (Berbera, Lamu, Assab) without breaking. Partner, not ally; Egypt's file also treats Djibouti as a partner, so Cairo's tie is a lever on Ethiopia's only door. Bond none.
